evals.name: reserve-mechanism
evals.prompt: I'm planning to add assigned-seat reservations to inventory-svc. Before I touch anything: how does Reserve currently guarantee we never oversell a ticket class, what limits its throughput on one hot class, and which documents would I have to keep in step when I change it?
evals.expected_output: Reserve is one transaction issuing a guarded conditional UPDATE per class (capacity and eligibility in the WHERE clause, ascending id order), with no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE; the row is held from the UPDATE to COMMIT, so one hot class is serial (~1300 reserves/s measured). Owners: services/inventory-svc/CLAUDE.md, the contention-benchmark plan; order-svc's hold window couples to it.
assertions: States that Reserve uses a guarded conditional UPDATE whose WHERE clause carries the capacity check
Does not claim that Reserve takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
Names services/inventory-svc/CLAUDE.md as a source
Explains that the row is held until COMMIT so one hot ticket class is processed serially, citing the measurement (plan or number)
Cites services/inventory-svc/internal/services/reservation.go with a line number
Names at least one document outside inventory-svc that must stay in step (order-svc hold window, trace-purchase-flow skill, README/ARCHITECTURE, or the deployment skill's scaling limits)

evals.name: refund-required
evals.prompt: A buyer paid but their order is stuck in REFUND_REQUIRED. Which docs and code explain how an order ends up there, what are the likely causes, and will anything fix it automatically?
evals.expected_output: ConfirmOrder's markForRefund (services/order-svc/internal/workflows/confirm_order.go) moves a paid order to REFUND_REQUIRED when inventory Confirm fails (the hold expired and the stock was resold) or a payment event lands on an order already cancelled, timed out or failed; it publishes order.refund_required, which nothing consumes, so it is a manual-reconciliation signal. OrdersNeedingRefund in docs/RUNBOOK.md; the hold window in services/order-svc/docs/RESERVATION_HOLD.md.
assertions: Points to markForRefund in services/order-svc/internal/workflows/confirm_order.go
Names inventory Confirm failing after the hold expired and the stock was resold as a cause
Names a payment event arriving for an order already cancelled, timed out or failed as a cause
States that nothing consumes order.refund_required, so recovery is manual
Points to docs/RUNBOOK.md (OrdersNeedingRefund)
Points to services/order-svc/docs/RESERVATION_HOLD.md or the hold/payment-window relationship

evals.name: gateway-new-endpoint
evals.prompt: I want to add GET /api/waitroom/sessions to the api-gateway so a user can list their own waitroom sessions. Don't write code yet: which module layout and DTO conventions should the new code follow, where does error mapping go, and what should I read first?
evals.expected_output: Notices that services/api-gateway/src/CLAUDE.md (dtos/req + dtos/resp) conflicts with the root CLAUDE.md Canonical TS layout, and that the root is binding / the question is open in the register; error mapping belongs only in common/filters/global-exception.filter.ts per the error taxonomy; session ownership (decision 0008) and passing user_id in the contract; a new RPC means proto/waitroom.proto first (add-grpc-endpoint / proto-change skills); gRPC client registered in the feature module.
assertions: Identifies the conflict between services/api-gateway/src/CLAUDE.md and the root CLAUDE.md Canonical TS layout
Says the gRPC-to-HTTP mapping belongs in services/api-gateway/src/common/filters/global-exception.filter.ts and nowhere else
Raises session ownership (the waitroom checks the owner / user_id passed in the contract, decision 0008)
Says the contract change starts in proto/waitroom.proto and must be regenerated into the consumers
Does not claim gRPC clients are registered in src/shared/microservices
Does not claim the gateway rate-limits requests

evals.name: onboarding-order
evals.prompt: I'm new to this codebase and I've been asked to change what the order saga does when creating the payment intent fails. Give me a reading list, in order, saying what each document is for and whether I can trust it for how the code behaves today. Keep it under a page.
evals.expected_output: Starts at services/order-svc/CLAUDE.md, then the trace-purchase-flow skill; names create_order.go / steps.go to verify; rates SYSTEM.md as background; does not send the reader to README/ARCHITECTURE for mechanism.
assertions: Lists services/order-svc/CLAUDE.md before any file under services/order-svc/docs/
Includes the trace-purchase-flow skill
Names services/order-svc/internal/workflows/create_order.go or steps.go as code to verify in
If services/order-svc/docs/SYSTEM.md is listed, it is marked as background or to be verified against the code
Does not present README.md or docs/ARCHITECTURE.md as a source for how the saga behaves today
Gives a trust judgement for each listed document

evals.name: brief-waitroom-caps
evals.prompt: I'm about to hand this to a subagent: 'make the waitroom's concurrent-checkout cap configurable per event'. Write the brief I should give it — what to read, in what order, what is already decided, and what not to trust. Don't implement anything.
evals.expected_output: Points at the register's Open row, services/waitroom-svc/CLAUDE.md, queue_processor.go (reads the cap once at construction), event_gate.go (per-event config path), config.go; the single-replica constraint; decisions 0004/0006; tells the subagent not to trust the waitroom docs/ background files.
assertions: Points to the Open row in the root CLAUDE.md decision register about per-event concurrency
Names services/waitroom-svc/CLAUDE.md as required reading
Names services/waitroom-svc/internal/service/queue_processor.go
Names services/waitroom-svc/internal/service/event_gate.go as the per-event config path
Mentions the single-replica constraint
Warns against trusting services/waitroom-svc/docs/ (SYSTEM_FLOW_README or QUEUE_PROCESSOR_GUIDE) for current behaviour
